findings: Input, launch and close intents precede dispatch. Unknown state blocks every new input and task removal; explicit no-effect clearing requires the actual ControlError class, one of eight source-bound preinput codes, restoration/no-unknown/no-retry and a post-error Main guard.

Known launch receipt/topology is recorded before later read-only observation, avoiding false unknown-launch labeling. Normal removal is limited to its exact owned leaf and preserves the full baseline task topology; the close pending state survives errors.

Click ACK compares each fresh selector field against actual_target. Actual a536 ActionRunner computes characters with Java String.codePointCount, so Python len(value) correctly includes the non-BMP emoji as one code point for this fixture. Set-text also requires native exact readback and observed after-state.

The diagnostic chain retains contiguous guest-time event coverage and only accepts a new normal-close exit for the exact sampled PID with reason10/subreason22/status0/description remove task. Existing Core13 raw-format test is explicitly separated from synthesized Probe device fixtures.
CE/DE inode and bounded model-content hashes are read only with no-follow/no-atime fences. Final identity/data/strict Main equality and all three controlled rounds are required.

One 45-second cleanup reserve is armed once; any scope, cleanup or context-exit exception prevents success. The sampler must stop/join, and per-round coverage/resource limits are checked only after both session contexts exit.

Runtime resource evidence does not automatically qualify complete engine mapping or long-duration stability. Existing 8 tests were inspected, not rerun; all UI/runtime boundary doubles and the real host-file no-follow checks are identified in the test source.
limitations: No stage, device call, native input or actual Probe round was performed by this review.
The review is bound to the two exact source hashes above, not future edits or whole-App production readiness.
Initial boundary-harness attempts remain separate historical files; they are not App failures.
